questions.question:
Rs. 6000 is lent at the annual rate of 10 percent for 2 years. Which of the following is statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Simple interest to be received on this sum is Rs. 1200

II. Compound Interest (compounding annually) to be received on this sum is Rs. 1260

options.text: Both statement I and II are correct

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal amount (P) = Rs. 6000

Rate of interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time period (t) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

I. Simple Interest (S.I.) = (P * R * t) / 100

II. Compound Interest (C.I.) = P * [1 + (R/100)]^t - P

where, P is the principal amount, R is the rate of interest, t is the time period.

For annual compounding, t = number of years.

**Solution:**

I. Simple Interest = (P * R * t) / 100

= (6000 * 10 * 2) / 100

= Rs. 1200

Therefore, statement I is correct.

II. Compound Interest = P * [1 + (R/100)]^t - P

= 6000 * [(1 + (10/100))² - 1]

= 6000 * [(1.1)² - 1]

= 6000 * [1.21 - 1]

= 6000 * 0.21

= Rs. 1260

Therefore, statement II is also correct.

Hence, both statement I and statement II are correct.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A man borrows a sum of Rs. 12,000 which amounts to Rs. 13,200 in 2 years on simple interest. What would have been the amount if the rate of interest was doubled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the rate of interest when Principal and Time are constant.

Original Simple Interest = Rs. 13,200 − Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

If the rate of interest is doubled, the Simple Interest will also be doubled.

New Simple Interest = 2 × 1,200 = Rs. 2,400

New Amount = Principal + New Interest = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Amount in 2 years (A) = Rs. 13,200

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = A − P

I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da3a82cf7318b08ad6307d87c03469ea7a1bef468aa7f1c8d3155d0f1097ca39.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original Interest = 13,200 − 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

⇒ 1,200 = (12,000 × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,200 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 1,200 ÷ 240 = 5%

⇒ New Rate = 2 × 5% = 10%

⇒ New Interest = (12,000 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100 = Rs. 2,400

⇒ New Amount = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal (P), Rate (R), and Time (T). If any one of these is multiplied by a factor while the others remain constant, the Simple Interest is simply multiplied by the same factor.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the original principal every year, meaning it remains constant per period. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the original principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Simple Interest Formula

The formula to calculate simple interest is I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. The total amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + I.
</p

questions.question: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Rs. 403 in 3 years at the rate of 10% per annum, What is the value of the sum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total simple interest percentage for 3 years = 3 × 10% = 30%.

The total Amount becomes 100% (Principal) + 30% (Interest) = 130%.

Principal from Amount Rule

When only the final amount (A) is given in simple interest, the principal (P) can be found directly using: P = (A × 100) ÷ (100 + R × T).

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, whereas compound interest is calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Effective Rate Concept

For simple interest, the effective rate for multiple years is simply the product of Rate and Time (Effective Rate = R × T %). This allows direct percentage-based calculations without using the standard long formulas.

questions.question: How much time (in years) will it take for an amount of ₹4,50,000 to yield ₹45,000 as simple interest at a 5% per annum rate of interest?
questions.solution:

Principal (P) = ₹4,50,000

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹45,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 5% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

We need to find T, so we rearrange the formula:

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ T = (SI × 100) / (P × R)

⇒ T = (45,000 × 100) / (4,50,000 × 5)

⇒ T = 45,00,000 / 22,50,000

⇒ T = 2 years

**It will take 2 years for an amount of ₹4,50,000 to yield ₹45,000 as simple interest at a 5% per annum rate of interest.**

questions.question:
A total of ₹2,00,000 is divided into two parts for investing in different banks on simple interest. One yields 4% p.a. while the

other yields 6% p.a. If the total interest at the end of one year is equivalent to 4.7% p.a. on the whole amount, the amount (in

₹) invested in each bank is ________, respectively.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By using the mixture and alligation rule directly on the interest rates:

Ratio of investments = (6% − 4.7%) : (4.7% − 4%) = 1.3 : 0.7 = 13 : 7

Total parts = 13 + 7 = 20 parts ≡ ₹2,00,000

Amount in 4% bank (13 parts) = (13 ÷ 20) × 2,00,000 = ₹1,30,000

Amount in 6% bank (7 parts) = (7 ÷ 20) × 2,00,000 = ₹70,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,30,000 and ₹70,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total principal = ₹2,00,000

Interest rate of Bank 1 = 4% p.a.

Interest rate of Bank 2 = 6% p.a.

Overall equivalent rate = 4.7% p.a. for 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ccea50f1a263967c2a5efa52594c3a5bf6fa5704ac4a02a49ef7beb0c13f6fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total interest earned at 4.7% = (2,00,000 × 4.7 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹9,400

⇒ Let the principal invested in Bank 1 be ₹x. Thus, the principal in Bank 2 will be ₹(2,00,000 − x).

⇒ Total Interest = Interest from Bank 1 + Interest from Bank 2

⇒ [(x × 4 × 1) ÷ 100] + [((2,00,000 − x) × 6 × 1) ÷ 100] = 9400

⇒ 4x + 12,00,000 − 6x = 9,40,000

⇒ 2x = 12,00,000 − 9,40,000

⇒ 2x = 2,60,000

⇒ x = ₹1,30,000

⇒ Investment in Bank 2 = 2,00,000 − 1,30,000 = ₹70,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,30,000 and ₹70,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mixtures and Alligations

It is an analytical method used to find the ratio in which two quantities must be mixed to obtain a desired average value. Rule: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Average Price) ÷ (Average Price − Price of Cheaper).

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the original principal amount. The principal remains constant throughout the tenure. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Overall / Effective Interest Rate

When multiple investments are made at different interest rates, the overall interest rate is the weighted average of the individual rates based on the amount of capital invested in each scheme.

questions.question: If a sum of ₹5,000 is taken at a simple rate of interest of 15% per annum for 3 years and another sum of ₹8,000 is taken at a simple interest of 12% per annum for 4 years, the positive difference of the interests paid is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest percentage for the first sum = 15% × 3 = 45%

Interest on the first sum = 45% of 5000 = ₹2,250

Effective interest percentage for the second sum = 12% × 4 = 48%

Interest on the second sum = 48% of 8000 = ₹3,840

Positive difference = 3840 − 2250 = 1590

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,590.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P₁ = ₹5,000, R₁ = 15%, T₁ = 3 years

P₂ = ₹8,000, R₂ = 12%, T₂ = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (5000 × 15 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₁ = 50 × 45 = ₹2,250

⇒ SI₂ = (8000 × 12 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 80 × 48 = ₹3,840

⇒ Difference = SI₂ − SI₁

⇒ Difference = 3840 − 2250 = ₹1,590

Compound Interest Formula

The accumulated amount over T years is calculated using the formula A = P(1 + R/100)T.

SI vs CI Difference

For exactly 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal is P(R/100)². For 3 years, the exact difference formula is P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Rule of 72

A well-known approximation stating that the time needed to double an investment at a compound rate of R% is roughly 72 ÷ R years.
